BiblicalUsage: Deceit — the thorns in the parable of the sower, choking the word with the deceitfulness of riches; the old man corrupted by deceitful lusts; and sin itself, which hardens hearts by deceiving them day after day. The word never describes an honest mistake; it describes a lure.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that deceit is dangerous precisely because it feels good while it works. Riches promise security, lust promises life, and sin promises freedom, and I believe only the daily honesty of God's word keeps me from believing any of them.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
